subject: English

source.title: National curriculum in England: English programmes of study

rules.ks1Progression: The programme is specified year-by-year, but schools have flexibility over when content is introduced within the key stage.
rules.ks2Progression: The programme is specified in two-year blocks; schools remain responsible for covering the relevant programme by the end of the key stage.
rules.ks3Ks4: English content is organised as key-stage programmes rather than fabricated statutory year-by-year sequences.

KS1.summary: Listen and respond appropriately, speak clearly for different purposes and audiences, participate in discussion, and build vocabulary through spoken language.
Develop accurate word reading through phonics and other taught strategies, build fluency, and understand and discuss stories, poems, plays and information texts.
Develop transcription, spelling, handwriting and sentence construction, and compose narratives, poetry and non-fiction for appropriate purposes and audiences.
Develop understanding and use of word classes, sentence structures, vocabulary, punctuation and standard English appropriate to the key-stage programme.

KS2.summary: Listen and respond effectively, ask relevant questions, build on others' contributions, present ideas clearly, and participate in discussions, debates and performances.
Read fluently and widely across fiction, poetry, plays and non-fiction; develop vocabulary, comprehension, inference, comparison and justification using evidence.
Plan, draft, revise and edit writing for different purposes and audiences, developing coherent composition, accurate transcription and increasingly effective vocabulary and structure.
Use and explain increasingly varied grammatical structures, vocabulary, punctuation and standard English, applying the required spelling knowledge and terminology.

KS3.summary: Develop confident spoken communication through speeches, presentations, formal debates, structured discussion, drama and performance, adapting language to audience and purpose.
Read increasingly challenging fiction and non-fiction independently, including significant English and world literature, and analyse vocabulary, inference, structure, context and evidence.
Write accurately and effectively for a range of purposes and audiences, selecting vocabulary, structure and tone, and planning, drafting, evaluating and editing work.
Consolidate grammatical knowledge, vocabulary and punctuation and apply standard English accurately to support clear and effective communication.

KS4.summary: Speak confidently and effectively in formal and informal contexts, adapting language and presentation to purpose and audience and responding constructively to others.
Read and understand challenging literary and non-fiction texts, analyse language, form and structure, make informed interpretations, and support responses with precise textual references.
Write accurately, fluently and effectively for different purposes and audiences, organising ideas coherently and selecting vocabulary, tone and rhetorical methods appropriately.
Apply accurate spelling, punctuation, grammar and standard English, using language choices deliberately to communicate meaning and achieve intended effects.

statementPolicy: Objectives are concise TEACHR paraphrases of the statutory programme structure, not substitutes for the official source text. The official GOV.UK publication remains authoritative. Example content and non-statutory notes must not be represented as statutory requirements.
